findings.title: Punishment as a bounded public sign
findings.claim: The pericope makes consequence bounded in both form and audience: the focus specifies bodily or territorial responses, and the altered body or removed place can function as a warning addressed beyond the offender.
findings.mechanism: The focus carrier جَزَٰٓؤُا۟ heads a finite sequence of killing, hanging, cutting, and removal. The 5:31 body-treatment context and the 5:38 recompense, cutting, and deterrent wording activate the relation in which a specified consequence becomes a public sign rather than undirected retaliation.
findings.reader_payoff: The list becomes legible as measured consequence with a visible social address, while each listed form remains a live option in the focus.
findings.containment: This does not decide which listed response applies, does not make deterrence the sole purpose of punishment, and does not replace the ordinary legal meaning of the focus.

epistemic.reason: The channel supports and focus wording are trusted, but several admitted branch images are nominated rather than supplied as registered lexical branches.
